bug_semantics: Scriban built-ins string.pad_left and string.pad_right (StringFunctions.PadLeft/PadRight) pass a caller-controlled width straight to .NET String.PadLeft/PadRight with no cap. An untrusted template such as {{ '' | string.pad_left 500000000 }} forces a ~1GB UTF-16 allocation and can throw OutOfMemoryException. TemplateContext.LimitToString is enforced only later in ObjectToString after the padded string already exists, so it does not stop the CWE-770 denial of service.
flaw_origin: The unbounded two-arg wrappers were first written in 779161586560786e835d27bffe70016357e980d8 (PR #70, 2018-09-10) as thin BCL delegates; parent 68fc3aa26b24e6a5b4cdfd87b93ad53b6539caa1 has no string pad builtins. Those same bodies remain at 6.6.0. 4227fdee198e7176ff974cfee13dc300f5babe9d (first released in 7.0.0) marks the two-arg overloads [ScriptMemberIgnore] and adds TemplateContext overloads that reject width > LimitToString via VerifyPaddingWidth before PadLeft/PadRight run.
